Embedding Media in Your Pages

This guide covers three ways to embed media content: native HTML elements, third-party player iframes, and platform-specific embed codes.

Using the iframe element

Many video platforms provide an embed code that uses <iframe> to load a player from their servers: 

<iframe
  src="https://example-player.test/embed/abc123"
  title="Introduction video"
  width="640"
  height="360"
  allowfullscreen
></iframe>

Note that the <iframe> element requires a descriptive title attribute so screen reader users can identify the embedded content before navigating into it.

Using the native video element

For self-hosted files, use the native <video> element. Unlike an <iframe>, the native element gives you direct control over track elements, captions, and audio descriptions.

Choosing between iframe and native video

  • Use an <iframe> when you want to delegate player controls, progress tracking, and CDN delivery to a third-party platform.
  • Use <video> for direct control over accessibility features — captions (<track kind="captions">) and audio descriptions are easiest to manage natively.
